title: The existing normalized completed pullback as one record
statement: Fix the prime and finite coefficient extension and a scheme morphism f:X to Y. Use the unrestricted completed coefficient module categories [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and localization q of flat-term K-flat representatives. Package the normalized completed pullback of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] as a record (F,e,U), where F:D(Y) to D(X), e:q followed by F is naturally isomorphic to the actual pullback-on-good-complexes functor, and U says: for every other G and normalization d:q followed by G isomorphic to that same functor there exists a unique isomorphism i:F to G whose restriction followed by d equals e. The concrete record takes the exact functor and comparison already chosen by integralDerivedPullback and integralDerivedPullbackComparison and their existing universal property. Those existing definitions are the two projections of this record. Reducing the projections gives the exact old terms; no data choice or mathematical statement is changed.

source.place: Tag 099N(5); Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.9(4); the existing normalized descent integralOperationsWellDefined, with the same record pattern as IntegralCompletedTensorDescent.

proof.text: Use the existing first functor witness and its existing comparison witness, without making a new choice. The universal field is the first conjunct of the existing well-definedness theorem after eliminating the remaining tensor functor and comparison. The functor and comparison projections of this concrete record reduce to the exact former bodies. Its universal property determines the record up to unique compatible isomorphism. This is a packaging of proved normalized descent, including for the zero complex and arbitrary scheme morphisms, not an added hypothesis.
